china_race_dynamics.text: The influx of data centers across our Commonwealth and our country present a unique challenge. [...] At the same time, the U.S. has a vested national security interest in ensuring we have the requisite facilities to compete technologically with China. [...] That’s why I believe that any data center being built needs to have support from the local community with no exceptions, cannot raise electricity costs by one cent on any other rate payer, and must have a closed-loop water system to prevent massive water use that negatively impacts the surrounding community.

deepseek.reason: The speaker calls competing technologically with China a vested US national security interest justifying data center buildout.
deepseek.confidence_reason: Competition with China is explicitly framed as a national security priority, though the statement's focus is data center siting conditions.

astra.reason: She endorses facilities needed to compete with China while insisting on community, electricity-cost, and environmental safeguards.
astra.confidence_reason: Both the competitive objective and mandatory safeguards despite that objective are explicit.
